title: Unconfigured non-18-decimal token treated as 18-dec 1:1 (fail-open) — claim() drains a strategy's full yield for ~0 payment
rootCause: src/StableYieldAccumulator.sol _normalizeAmount L591-593 + _denormalizeAmount L622-624 fail-open fallback (decimals==0 && rate==0 => 18-dec 1:1 passthrough); claim() prices via normalize L489 -> discount L497 -> denormalize L498; addYieldStrategy L227 / setRewardToken L360 never require a TokenConfig.
summary: DRAIN: a 6-decimal strategy token registered via addYieldStrategy but left without setTokenConfig keeps its default (0,0) config, hitting the fail-open 18-dec passthrough. A 1,000e6 (6-dec) skimmed yield normalizes to 1000e6-as-18-dec, then denormalizes to the configured 6-dec reward token and floors to 0. Claimer receives the full 1000e6 yield and pays 0; phlimbo and SYA receive nothing; preview already advertises 0. CONTROL: the identical yield with the strategy token configured charges the full 1000e6 (all to phlimbo) — proving the gap is the single missing setTokenConfig, not the amount.

validation.notes: PoC imports and calls the real src/StableYieldAccumulator.sol claim(), which routes through _normalizeAmount L489 and _denormalizeAmount L498. Mocks are interface-faithful: SyaMockStrategy implements IYieldStrategy and skimSurplus performs a REAL ERC20 transfer of the underlying to the claimer (yield delivery is genuine, not faked); SyaMockPhlimbo.collectReward pulls via transferFrom; SyaMockNFTMinter.burn matches INFTMinter. The control test pays the full 1000e6 through the same mocks, proving payment routing is not rigged and the delta is exactly the one missing setTokenConfig.

verifiedMath.drain: strat token unconfigured (decimals==0 && rate==0) -> _normalizeAmount fail-open passthrough: 1000e6 stays 1000e6 (treated as 18-dec, understated 1e12x); discount 0 -> claimerPayment 1000e6; _denormalizeAmount to configured 6-dec reward: 1000e6 / 1e12 = 0 (floors). yield delivered 1000e6, payment 0.
verifiedMath.control: strat token configured (6,1e18): normalize 1000e6 -> 1000e18; denormalize to reward -> 1000e6. payment == yield == 1000e6, all to phlimbo.

validation.robustness: Drain holds for any sub-18-dec strategy token whenever the reward token has <18 decimals (the canonical USDC reward token per spec). Exact rewardPaid==0 holds for any single-claim skimmed yield under ~1e12 native units (~1,000,000 tokens at 6-dec); above that the payment is a negligible ~1e-12-of-value dust, so the drain still holds. The PoC's 1000-token amount sits firmly in the floor-to-0 regime. Not amount-fragile.
caveatsForReportWriter: Precondition: the drain's exact zero-payment requires the REWARD token to be configured with <18 decimals (PoC uses 6-dec USDC, matching the spec's canonical reward token). If the reward token were 18-dec the mispricing would manifest differently (not a clean zero). State this precondition explicitly.
Strict rewardPaid==0 is exact for per-claim yield below ~1,000,000 tokens (6-dec); for larger single claims the payment is dust (~1e-12 of value), still an effective drain.

PoC is NOT C4-standalone: it imports src/StableYieldAccumulator.sol and test/mocks/SYAMocks.sol via project remappings. This is correct/required for a workspace PoC run against the project suite; a C4 paste would require inlining src + mocks.
